audit_findings.title: Post-acquisition financing cost is missing from the pre-acquisition earnings numerator
audit_findings.magnitude: Interest expense increased by a filed $10.9 million for the first six months of 2026, from $16.9 million to $27.8 million; a simple annualization is $21.8 million, equal to 21.6% of the $100.7 million anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: The equity-level OE numerator retains interest expense, but the anchor predates the acquisition-related increase from $570 million to $1.0 billion of debt
audit_findings.evidence: The term loan facility was drawn on fully for the amount of $1.0 billion with proceeds used to refinance the outstanding term loan facility and to finance in part the acquisition of Koch Filter Corporation.
audit_findings.explanation: The financing mismatch is demonstrated: current shareholders bear the higher interest cost, while the modeled OE does not. The magnitude is large relative to anchor OE. Exclusion of Koch Filter earnings creates an offsetting omission, but it does not cure the missing financing cost or establish the net effect of moving to the current perimeter.
audit_findings.action: Rerun using post-acquisition Koch Filter operating results, maintenance capex and the recurring interest run rate from the 2026 credit facility; alternatively, consistently reconstruct both earnings and bridge on the pre-acquisition perimeter.

audit_findings.title: The equity-method stakes may be counted in both owner earnings and the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: Potential duplicated bridge addition of $89.2 million, equal to $1.08 per diluted share and 5.1% of the $1,763 million base equity value; the related 2025 investee-income line was $33.8 million, or 33.6% of anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Investee earnings can be capitalized in operating OE while the $89.2 million carrying value of the same stakes is also added through the equity bridge
audit_findings.evidence: Our share of the results from joint ventures, affiliated companies and alliances is reported in our Consolidated Statements of Net Income as “Equity, royalty and interest income from investees” and is reported net of all applicable income taxes.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved possibility rather than a demonstrated error because the supplied OE reconciliation does not show which components of equity, royalty and interest income were removed. The amounts are material enough to require resolution: retaining the earnings and adding the stake value duplicates the interests, while removing the earnings requires an independent economic valuation rather than automatically using book value.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $27.5 million equity-income component and $6.3 million royalty-and-interest component through 2025 OE, then rerun either with qualifying recurring earnings retained and no stake addition or with those earnings removed and the stakes independently valued.

audit_findings.title: The latest-year anchor may embed costs explicitly identified as nonrecurring
audit_findings.magnitude: Up to $21.6 million of potential 2025 OE normalization: $15.5 million of separation expense less its filed $3.4 million tax impact, plus $9.5 million of separation capital expenditures; this equals 21.4% of the $100.7 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: One-time expenses reduce net-income-based OE and one-time separation capital expenditures increase the capex deduction, depressing the anchor and all projected cash flows
audit_findings.evidence: During the year ended December 31, 2025, we incurred approximately $15.5 million related to one-time separation costs including $11.2 million within Cost of Sales and $4.3 million within Selling, general and administrative expenses.
audit_findings.explanation: The costs are filed and explicitly identified as one-time, but their inclusion in the $100.7 million anchor is not demonstrated without the OE worksheet. If both categories were included without normalization, the possible adjustment is large relative to anchor OE and could materially change the intrinsic-value range, although continuing standalone costs must remain.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the anchor line by line to net income, depreciation, working-capital treatment and capex; remove only the after-tax $15.5 million separation expense and the identified $9.5 million separation capex that actually entered OE, then rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Cash may not be fully distributable at face value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any inaccessible, required operating or tax-leaking cash would reduce the $259.0 million cash addition in the equity bridge
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2025, $ 181.3 million of non-U.S. earnings are considered indefinitely reinvested in operations outside the U.S. for which deferred taxes have not been provided.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes $181.3 million of indefinitely reinvested non-U.S. earnings, but that amount is accumulated earnings rather than identified cash. The record therefore does not demonstrate how much of the $259.0 million cash balance is foreign, restricted, operationally necessary or subject to repatriation leakage. The possible value effect cannot be established from the supplied numbers.
audit_findings.action: Obtain cash and short-term investments by legal entity and jurisdiction, restrictions, minimum operating-liquidity requirements and estimated withholding or repatriation taxes; rerun the bridge using only verified excess distributable cash.

audit_findings.title: The stated share-count ceiling is not a true maximum
audit_findings.magnitude: The modeled 82.797842 million shares exceed the July 31, 2026 outstanding count of 81.595527 million by exactly 1.202315 million, matching the filed year-end RSU/PSU inventory; even if every unit were a PSU receiving one additional share, the omitted dilution would be at most 1.202315 million shares, or 1.45% of the modeled denominator, reducing base value by about $0.30 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Above-target PSU settlement and related share equivalents increase the diluted-share denominator and reduce value per share
audit_findings.evidence: The final award may equal 0 - 200 percent of the target grant, based on our actual performance during the vesting period.
audit_findings.explanation: The word ceiling is incorrect because PSUs can settle at 200% of target. Nevertheless, an extreme upper bound using the entire filed RSU/PSU inventory as though all units were PSUs changes the modeled per-share value by only about 1.4%, far below the gap between the $21.29 base value and the $48.34 market price. Later awards are not quantified, but the latest filed diluted weighted-average count of 82.0 million is below the valuation denominator.
audit_findings.action: Relabel the denominator as a target-award fully diluted count and separately disclose contractual-maximum PSU shares, dividend equivalents and post-year-end grants in the next routine share-count update.

audit_findings.title: An underfunded pension claim may be absent from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed pension liabilities of $13.8 million less pension assets of $2.3 million produce an $11.5 million net claim, equal to $0.14 per diluted share and 0.65% of the $1,763 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: A residual underfunded pension claim would be deducted in the equity bridge if it is not already captured through OE or another bridge item
audit_findings.evidence: The liabilities were $ 13.8 million and $ 11.0 million as of December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively, and are reflected in the Consolidated Financial Statements as a component of Other liabilities.
audit_findings.explanation: The balance-sheet claim is identifiable, although its omission from the bridge is not conclusively established. Even deducting the full filed net deficit reduces base value by only about $0.14 per share and cannot change the valuation conclusion relative to the $48.34 market price.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the June 30, 2026 net funded status, required contributions and whether any amount is already reflected elsewhere; deduct only the residual net claim during the next bridge update.
